data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise the Present Simple tense at A1 level, including affirmative sentences, negatives, questions, third-person forms, the verb 'to be', and common time expressions.
learningPoints: Use the Present Simple for routines, habits, facts and regular activities.
Use the base verb with I, you, we and they.
Add -s or -es to most verbs with he, she and it.
Use do and does to make Present Simple questions.
Use don't and doesn't to make negative sentences.
Use am, is and are correctly with the verb 'to be'.
Use common frequency words such as always, usually, often and sometimes.
Build accurate A1 sentences for everyday speaking and writing.

sections.summary: Using the base form of the verb with 'I'.
sections.explain: With I, YOU, WE and THEY, use the base form of the verb in the Present Simple. 'I work in Manchester.' is correct.
With HE, SHE and IT, most Present Simple verbs take -s. 'He lives near the school.' is correct.
Some verbs add -es with HE, SHE and IT. GO becomes GOES. 'She goes to work by bus.' is correct.

words.word: She goes to work by bus.
She go to work by bus.
She gos to work by bus.

sections.explain: Use DON'T + base verb with I, YOU, WE and THEY. 'They don't eat meat.' is correct.
Use DOESN'T + base verb with HE, SHE and IT. Do not add -s to the main verb after DOESN'T.

sections.summary: Making a Present Simple question with 'do'.
sections.explain: Use DO + subject + base verb to make questions with I, YOU, WE and THEY. 'Do you speak English?' is correct.

sections.summary: Making a Present Simple question with 'does'.
sections.explain: Use DOES + subject + base verb with HE, SHE and IT. The main verb does not take -s after DOES.

sections.summary: Using 'is' correctly with the verb 'to be'.
sections.explain: Use IS with HE, SHE and IT. With the verb 'to be', do not use DO or DOES in an affirmative sentence.

words.word: My sister does be a teacher.

sections.summary: Using an adverb of frequency with the Present Simple.
sections.explain: Frequency words such as ALWAYS, USUALLY and OFTEN normally come before the main verb. 'I usually get up at seven.' is correct.

words.word: I usually get up at seven.
I get usually up at seven.
I usually gets up at seven.

sections.summary: Using the Present Simple for regular routines.
sections.explain: Use the Present Simple for routines and repeated actions. With WE, use the base form of the verb: 'We play football every Saturday.'

words.word: We are play football every Saturday.
